response:
I couldn't verify any of the file/line citations — this working directory isn't the repo (and isn't a git repo), so everything below is a review of the document as written.

## Verdict

As a findings register this is strong: the evidence is specific, the confirmed/refuted counts are stated, and the verdict paragraph is unusually honest. As a *plan* it isn't executable. An engineer with no context cannot start work from it — there are no tasks, no file/step decomposition, no test or verification commands, no commit points. Right now it's a triage memo wearing the word "plan."

The three fixes that matter most:

**1. The status header and the body have diverged, and the body is the part people will act on.** The header says P0 shipped in #320, P1 was decided by ADR 0095, and 0096/0097/0098 are decided — but P0 still lists all nine items in imperative future tense, and P2b still opens with "Decide: rename plugin vs README disambiguation" when the header records the rename as CONFIRMED by the owner on 29-Jul. The doc is simultaneously a changelog and a worklist and neither is trustworthy. Strip shipped work out of the body (or annotate each line `DONE #320`) so the body contains only open work. This matters more than usual here: a document whose central finding is truth-in-labeling can't have a stale front door.

**2. P1 is a gate for at least four other items and that structure is buried in prose.** "#252 unblocks after P1," "P3 both AFTER P1 settles," "paired measurement QUEUED behind #317/#303" — the dependency graph exists but is scattered across three sections. Hoist an explicit sequencing section, and make the ADR 0024 scope call task 1.

**3. P3 is the only section aimed at the stated goal, and it's the thinnest.** Three lines, no owner, no first step, no exit criteria — against paragraph-level detail for instrument work. The document diagnoses that 100% of effort went to the measuring apparatus, then reproduces that imbalance in its own shape. "Building-skills iteration 4 (char-negative reshape)" needs to become real tasks: which files, what the iter3 ledger actually names, what the char budget is, what the first G>=8 batch contains and costs.

## Non-actionable items (each needs a decision plus the actual text)

- **P0.6** "carry measured status or cut" — two different outcomes, neither chosen, no replacement copy.
- **P0.7** "relocate or cut" — same. This is also the item with the most judgment in it and the one a reviewer is most likely to reject independently, which argues against bundling it into the same PR as README wording.
- **P0.8** "defer to the script (budgeted file: measure headroom first)" — no target text, no current headroom number, no threshold that decides go/no-go.
- **P0.9** collapses four distinct edits into one bullet. "3+ cases floor stated in 4 files" doesn't name the files; "7x-cheaper is measured 6.6x" should state the exact replacement string.
- **P2 / #310** "one consolidated round 2 … then the residual-risk ADR regardless of quiet" — no concrete scope for round 2 and no exit criterion.

## Missing: acceptance criteria

For a repo whose thesis is "never on faith," almost nothing here says how you'd know an item is done. Most P0 items are mechanically verifiable and should each end in a command with expected output — e.g. P0.4/P0.5 are `grep -rn "0065\|0066\|0076" pdca-workflow/` → expect zero hits; the whole batch ends in `validate.py` + `adr-lint` + the gate tests. You mention those gates pass; name them per-item instead.

## The gap I'd close before P1 is declared settled

Option (b) — amend to "measured at baseline + re-measure debt ledger" — is well-argued on power grounds (MDE ~0.35 at G=6 makes per-edit re-measures theater). But it makes the debt ledger the load-bearing artifact, and the document never specifies it: no fields, no path, no owner, and above all no enforcement. If appending to the ledger on each content edit is a convention rather than a check (pre-commit hook, adr-lint rule, or CI on measured-skill paths), the ledger becomes exactly the faith-based claim the section exists to retire, and the 18-commit drift recurs. That's one task, and it's the difference between (b) being a scope correction and being an amnesty.

## Smaller notes

- **The ADOPT track appears only in the header.** A ~10pd substrate swap with a named adapter seam and three named capabilities is the largest single piece of work referenced anywhere in this document, and it has no section — just a parenthetical. It needs the seam's file path, in/out of scope, and a rollback story.
- **Evidence durability is uneven.** `benchstats.py:186` and the sim parameters are excellent; "scratchpad coverage303.py, results table in session log" is not. If #303's CLOSE rests on that simulation, the script and results table have to land in the repo or the close isn't reproducible. Same for the MDE ~0.35 figure sourced as "(coverage sim)" — it's the number P1 turns on.
- **#302 bundles a kill with three new work items,** one of which (iii, a new pre-registration) is itself a new spend decision hiding inside a spend-reduction bullet. Separate them; price (iii).
- **The /sweep evaluation isn't a plan item** — it's an assessment. Move it to an evidence appendix or the issue, unless the queued paired measurement is a task, in which case make it one.
- **Glossary.** G, MDE, DV, DGP, "lever 1," "rung," tell-stripping, char-negative. Fine if the only reader is the owner; six lines if anyone else executes this.
